title.en: THE STORY OF THE THREE BEARS
THE STORY OF THE THREE BEARS

extra.en:
THE STORY OF THE THREE BEARS
A BreakCraft sample adaptation
Public domain folk tale, freely retold

text.en: A tidy stone cottage sits deep in the woods, smoke curling from its chimney into the cool morning air. A well-worn path leads up to a round front door, painted a cheerful green.
Three bowls of PORRIDGE steam on the table: one large, one middling, one small. PAPA BEAR, MAMA BEAR and BABY BEAR gather round, spoons ready, napkins already tucked in.
Too hot to sit still for. Every morning the same trouble.
A walk while it cools, then, same as every morning. It's hardly a hardship.
already at the door
Last one to the stream carries the honey jar all the way back!
That was my honey jar last time, and the time before that.
already following Baby Bear out
Then perhaps walk a little faster this morning, dear.
The door swings shut behind them, their voices fading down the forest path. The porridge sits, cooling, in the quiet.

Some distance off, a girl with tangled GOLD HAIR wanders the same stretch of forest, humming to herself, clearly enjoying being lost rather more than she's worried about it. This is GOLDILOCKS, small, curious, and entirely unbothered by whose woods these are.
She spots the cottage's chimney smoke rising above the trees and changes direction toward it without a second thought.
Someone's home. Someone's home might know the way back to the village.
Goldilocks peers through the kitchen window, knocks twice on the green door, and lets herself in when no one answers, calling out a polite hello that no one is present to hear.
The three bowls of porridge sit untouched on the table. She tastes the large bowl first.
Too hot.
She tastes the middling bowl next, wrinkling her nose slightly.
Too cold. Whoever made this left far too long ago.
She tastes the small bowl, and empties it entirely before she notices she's done so.
Just right. Just right is a rare thing to find, honestly.
She sets the empty bowl down with a small, satisfied sigh, and wanders further into the cottage.
Three CHAIRS face a cold hearth: one broad and high-backed, one cushioned and low, one small and plainly made. Goldilocks tries the large one first, climbing up with some effort.
Far too firm. Whoever sits here must never relax at all.
She climbs down and tries the middling chair, sinking further than expected into its cushions.
Too soft, and lopsided besides. One leg's shorter than the others, I'd wager.
The small chair fits perfectly, right up until it doesn't - one leg gives way beneath her with a sharp crack, and she tips gently backward onto the rug, more startled than hurt.
from the floor
Oh, bother. That one's broken now, I'm afraid.
She picks herself up, dusts off her skirts, and continues her exploration further into the cottage as though nothing at all had happened.

A narrow wooden stairway climbs to the upper floor. Goldilocks pauses at the bottom, glancing back once toward the front door, then shrugs and climbs on up, curiosity plainly winning out over caution.
Three BEDS, largest to smallest, each neatly made. Goldilocks climbs onto the large one first, bouncing experimentally.
Too hard. Like sleeping on a stack of firewood.
She tries the middling bed next, sinking almost out of sight into its deep quilts.
Too soft. I'd never find my way out again.
The small bed is exactly right, and within moments she is fast asleep beneath its patchwork quilt, one arm trailing off the edge, entirely at ease.
The three bears amble homeward, Baby Bear trailing a stick along the ground, the honey jar swinging from Papa Bear's paw after all.
Breakfast should be just the right temperature by now.
It always is, if you're patient enough to let it cool properly.
The three bears return, unhurried, until Papa Bear stops short at the sight of the table.
Someone's had a taste of my porridge.
Someone's had a taste of mine, too, and left it a good deal messier than they found it.
staring into his empty bowl
Someone's finished all of mine! Every single spoonful!
The bears move through to the sitting room. Papa Bear notices his chair's cushion askew; Mama Bear finds hers faintly dented on one side.
Someone's been sitting in my chair.
Someone's been sitting in mine as well.
discovering the wreckage
Someone's been sitting in mine, and broken it clean through!
They climb the stairs together, more curious now than concerned, and find the beds in various states of disturbance.
Someone's been lying in my bed.
Someone's been lying in mine, too.
Someone's asleep in my bed - and here she is!

Goldilocks wakes to three faces peering down at her, blinks once, takes a full second to understand the scene, and is out the window and across the garden before anyone can offer her a proper breakfast.
The three bears watch from the upstairs window as Goldilocks sprints across the garden and disappears into the tree line without a single backward glance.
Should we go after her?
I imagine she's learned quite enough for one morning.
watching her go
Well. At least she liked the porridge. That's more than I can say for some visitors.
Baby Bear surveys his broken chair with a philosophical sigh and begins, without being asked, to see what can be done about mending it.
